entities.summary:
Amaras Monastery is an Armenian Apostolic monastery near Sos in the Nagorno-Karabakh (Artsakh) region, traditionally linked to early Christianisation and to Mesrop Mashtots’s teaching of the Armenian alphabet. It functioned for centuries as a religious and educational centre on a contested Caucasian frontier.

Medieval and early modern patronage kept Amaras in Armenian sacred geography even as imperial borders shifted among Persian, Ottoman, and Russian spheres. Modern wars over Karabakh made the monastery a heritage symbol as well as a spiritual site.

Amaras illustrates how monastic institutions preserve language, liturgy, and memory under geopolitical pressure.
